pages.en:
“………………”

“………………”

The stare boring into my back hurts.

As my knife goes *tock, tock* through the tofu, Saber sits properly upon her knees,

watching me with that same expression all the while.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”
“……”
I feel her staring at me, and it hurts.
Saber is sitting Japanese-style while I cut the tofu…
…Staring at me with that expression of hers.

pages.ja:
『今まで通り学校には行く』。
そう切り出した後、セイバーとの口論はずっと平行線だった。
セイバーは勿論反対。
マスターをひとりにするのは危険だ、という。
しかし、こっちにだって生活がある。
pages.jaRuby:
『今まで通り学校には行く』。

pages.en:
*I’m going to school as usual.*

Ever since I began with that declaration, my argument with Saber has gone nowhere.

Naturally, Saber is opposed. She says it is dangerous to leave her Master alone.

But I have a life to live too.
pages.mirrorMoon:
‘I will go to school like usual.’
We never reached a compromise after I said that.
Saber objected, of course.
She says it is dangerous for me to be alone.
But I have my personal life too.

pages.ja:
学校を休んだら藤ねえが不審がるし、ずっと家に篭っていたら外で何が起きているか判らない。
それに、セイバーと外に出るという事は、他のマスターを警戒させる事でもあるのだ。
一人で外の様子を見る、というのもそれなりに成果はありそうだし、なにより。
pages.jaRuby:
学校を休んだら藤ねえが不審がるし、ずっと家に篭っていたら外で何が起きているか判らない。

pages.en:
If I miss school, Fuji will become suspicious. If I remain shut inside the house, I will never know what is happening outside.

Besides, going out with Saber would put the other Masters on their guard.

There may be something to gain from observing the town alone. And more importantly—
pages.mirrorMoon:
Fuji-nee will get suspicious if I skip school, and I won’t know what’s going on outside if I stay indoors.
And to go somewhere with Saber means warning other Masters.
I think the results will be good enough if I go out on my own. And most of all…

pages.ja:
「マスター同士の戦いは人目を避けるんだろ。なら日中は安全だ。よほど人気のないところに出向かない限り、仕掛けられる事はない」
セイバーはそれでも安心できないと反論した。
……正直、そこまで過保護にされるとカチンときちまって、こっちも意地になって“学校行く案”を主張し続けて、その結果がこれである。

pages.en:
“Battles between Masters are supposed to avoid witnesses, right? Then I’ll be safe during the day. No one will attack me unless I wander somewhere deserted.”

Saber replied that even so, she could not rest easy.

…Honestly, being coddled to that extent irritated me. I became stubborn and continued insisting upon the plan to attend school, and this is the result.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Masters fight where there are no people, right? Then I’ll be safe during the day. Nobody will attack me unless I go someplace deserted.”
But Saber insisted that it’s not going to be enough.
…Her excessive concern pissed me off, so I stubbornly insisted that I’m going to school, and this is the result.

pages.ja:
「……………………」
セイバーの視線が痛いのは、言うまでもなくセイバーが怒っているからだ。

pages.en:
“……………………”

Saber’s stare hurts for the obvious reason that Saber is angry.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”
Her glare feels like it’s burning into me.

pages.ja:
今日の教訓。
あいつは怒らせるとかなり根に持つ。しかも感情的になるんで手におえない。
つまり、今後は意地の張り合いにならないよう気をつけよう。

pages.en:
Today’s lesson:

When angered, she nurses a grudge. She also becomes emotional enough to be entirely unmanageable.

In other words, I must take care not to let our disagreements become contests of stubbornness in the future.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The moral of the story is…
She’ll bear a big grudge if you make her mad. And she gets out of hand because she is emotional.
So I should be careful not to act stubborn again.

」

“No. Talking to myself. This tofu is tough.”

“————”

…And she has ears like a hawk. She is not someone I want to fight a cold war against.

“…Man, you inflexible blockhead.”

”

呼び鈴のあと、玄関の開く音がする。
ついで、聞きなれた「お邪魔します」という桜の声。

pages.en:
“Hm? Is it that time already?”

After the doorbell, I hear the front door open.

Then comes Sakura’s familiar “Excuse me.”

“Huh? It’s that time already?”
After the doorbell, I hear the front door opening.
And I also hear the familiar tone of Sakura’s
voice saying “excuse me”.
voice.

pages.jaRuby: 「そっか。セイバーと長話してたもんだから、いつもより三十分ロスしたわけだ」
pages.en: “Of course. That discussion with Saber cost me half an hour, so I’m running later than usual.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Oh, so I lost 30 minutes while I was arguing with Saber.”

pages.en:
Even so, breakfast is nearly ready.

I considered serving bread because Saber would enjoy it, but decided against it because that would look like an attempt to curry favor.

The Japanese eat rice.

To counter the violence of the stare fixed upon me, I exert silent pressure of my own: when in Rome, do as the Romans do.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But breakfast is almost ready.
I thought about having bread to please Saber, but it seemed too much like bribery, so I changed my mind.
Japanese people eat rice.
I’ll counter her violent glare with pressure of “when in Rome, do as the Romans do”.

「おはようございます、セイバーさん。昨日はよく眠れましたか？」
「はい。慣れない部屋でしたが、この屋敷には慣れていましたので問題はありません」
……お、二人が話してる。
昨日はろくに話さなかったけど、一晩明けて桜も納得してくれたみたいだ。

“Good morning, Saber. Did you sleep well last night?”

“Yes. The room was unfamiliar, but I was already accustomed to this estate, so it presented no difficulty.”

…Oh. The two of them are talking.

They barely spoke yesterday, but after a night to consider matters, Sakura seems to have accepted her presence.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Good morning, Saber-san. Were you able to sleep well last night?”
“Yes. It was not a familiar room, but it was not a problem since I am familiar with this house.”
…Oh, they’re talking.
They didn’t talk much yesterday, but I guess Sakura’s gotten over it after one night.

“Sorry to keep you waiting. Shirou, where should I begin?”

“Mm, one serving platter and four plates. The salad is finished, so divide it between them however you like.”

“All right. Oh, are these German potatoes today? This is rather elaborate for breakfast, Shirou. Almost like Western food.”

“Sorry to keep you waiting, Senpai. What should I start with?”
“Can you get one big plate and four small ones? The salad’s done, so you can serve it.”
“Okay. Wow, we’re having German potato salad this morning?
You’re elaborate this morning, cooking Western food.”

With evident surprise, Sakura spoons the enormous helping of German potatoes onto the platter.

For the record, the salad is the only Western-style dish.

…And to reiterate, I did not yield beneath Saber’s pressure. I merely lost my nerve a little.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Sakura is surprised, but she scoops out the salad onto the big plate.
The salad is the only Western food I made.
…You have to understand, I’m not giving in to Saber. I’m just… proactively trying to clear the air between us.

That gesture belongs to the Sakura I know.

The shock I felt a moment ago recedes, and I breathe a quiet sigh of relief.

Even so, the unease remains.

If some impulse drove Shinji to tell Sakura about the Matou family, the Holy Grail War, and the battles between Masters, she would cease to be an outsider from that very moment.

I cannot allow that to happen.
pages.mirrorMoon:

…But he’s never done something this bad before.
About half a year ago, I spotted a bruise on Sakura’s arm.
I hit Shinji when I realized he’d done it
but he’s never punched a girl’s face!
But I’m still uneasy.
If on some impulse Shinji was to tell Sakura about the Matou family, the Holy Grail War, and the battle between the Masters, she would no longer be unrelated from that moment on.
I have to avoid that.
